question.problem:
Consider a right triangle inscribed in a semicircle of radius
$8.$ If the hypotenuse of the triangle lies along the diameter of the semicircle, what is the greatest possible perimeter ${P}_{\text{max}}$ of the triangle? Do not round the answer.

${P}_{\text{max}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We first draw a picture of the situation:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14196324/assets/538c49b44e4acba74ce5a55e93f67d06f0dc0a0d893f817659739cec5d34d020.png)

Let's call $l$ the length of one of the legs. By the Pythagorean theorem, the length of the other leg is $\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}.$

Therefore, the perimeter is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(l) & =16+l+\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $l$ is the length of a leg of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is $16,$ the permitted range of $l$ is $0<l<16.$

We want to maximize $P(l),$ so we need to compute the critical points. Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(l) & =1+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{(-2l)}{\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}} \\  & =1-\frac{l}{\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

and solving ${P}^{′}(l)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(l) & =0 \\ 1-\frac{l}{\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}} & =0 \\ \frac{l}{\sqrt{256-{l}^{2}}} & =1 \\ \sqrt{256-{l}^{2}} & =l \\ 256-{l}^{2} & ={l}^{2} \\ 2{l}^{2} & =256 \\ {l}^{2} & =128 \\ l & =8\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to confirm that $l=8\sqrt{2}$ does indeed give a maximum value of $P(l).$ To do this, we use the first derivative test. We write up a table of values:

| Interval | $(0,8\sqrt{2})$ | $8\sqrt{2}$ | $(8\sqrt{2},16)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $2$ | $$ | $12$ |
| ${P}^{′}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $-$ |
| $P$ | $↗$ | $\text{max}$ | $↘$ |

So, $l=8\sqrt{2}$ does indeed give a maximum, and the perimeter of the resulting triangle will be the largest possible.

Therefore, the greatest perimeter ${P}_{\text{max}}$ that a triangle can have is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{\text{max}}=P(8\sqrt{2}) & =16+8\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{256-(8\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =16+8\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{256-128} \\  & =16+8\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{128} \\  & =16+8\sqrt{2}+8\sqrt{2} \\  & =16+16\sqrt{2} \\  & =16(1+\sqrt{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
